input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds us (the Customer) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, of undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and unlimited territory, and it also bars acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback on every material term (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Redline deletes § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, with the narrowed fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete imposed on Customer in § 12.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted § 12.4; it also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete commitment. If some protection is genuinely needed, we could consider a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and no more than 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
